To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the new B4 model can fit laboratory test data on creep and shrinkage with a high accuracy and a small number of parameters, (b) it can fit the multi-decade bridge deflections with an accuracy that is sufficient for sustainable design of large structures and (c) it can be used for reliable prediction and quantification of uncertainty of multi-decade deflection and creep of large concrete structures.

Model B4 is the first model that is able to accurately and reliably predict multi-decade creep for a wide range of concrete strengths, and that it is the first model to predict multi-decade shrinkage for concrete of any strength, and that it does so using only the composition and strength as input.

Model B4, which is based on the B3 model, can be calibrated by a large worldwide database of individual laboratory creep and shrinkage test curves, which is combined with a database of bridge deflection data, to predict creep and shrinkage for a wide range of concrete compositions for 50 to 100 years.
